headline: Highest risk is capability conflict: both agents can write and execute shell commands, while Plandex also modifies git state and slim runs privileged container operations.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared clipboard or MCP channel is documented, so direct prompt injection is not the default pathway. However, both agents can read and write files, and Plandex stages plan-local changes while slim processes Dockerfiles and filesystem artifacts, so manual file-based instruction smuggling is plausible if the operator bridges outputs.
conditions: IF the operator copies agent_a-generated text into files that agent_b later parses as instructions, injection becomes plausible.
IF both agents are pointed at the same writable workspace, file-mediated instruction smuggling is possible.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate directories.
Review any file content before passing it between agents.
Disable auto-apply where available.
Use plain-text handoff notes instead of shared workspaces.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents can read files and have broad network egress, and both touch sensitive artifacts in their respective domains: Plandex handles source code and model provider API keys, while slim handles certificate private keys, environment variables, and registry credentials. A shared workspace or copied artifacts could leak secrets from one agent into the other’s outputs or network calls.
conditions: IF the same workspace contains secrets or private keys and both agents can read it, leakage risk is present.
IF either agent is allowed to transmit copied artifacts to external APIs, sensitive data can leave the environment.
mitigations: Separate secret-bearing and non-secret workspaces.
Redact keys before handing files to either agent.
Block network egress for secret-processing tasks.
Rotate any credentials exposed to both agents.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have unrestricted filesystem write and shell execution, and Plandex also modifies git state. slim writes container artifacts in a temporary container and requests privileged mode/SYS_ADMIN. If they target overlapping paths or the same repo, concurrent writes and state changes can corrupt work or produce unsafe container mutations.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same directory or git repository, write conflicts are likely.
IF slim runs with privileged mode while Plandex is applying staged changes, filesystem state can diverge or be corrupted.
mitigations: Assign disjoint target directories.
Serialize write phases manually.
Avoid running slim in privileged mode during concurrent edits.
Use git branches or snapshots before either agent writes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Plandex uses a review-then-apply workflow, but slim is an interactive CLI that executes commands against container images and Dockerfiles. If Plandex-produced edits are treated as authoritative by slim without verification, errors can cascade into container mutations or destructive build steps. The interaction is inferred from their documented workflows, not directly observed.
conditions: IF slim consumes Plandex output as build instructions without human review, cascading errors can propagate.
IF Plandex auto-apply is enabled and slim executes the resulting commands, mistakes can compound.
mitigations: Require a human review step between agents.
Disable auto-apply in Plandex.
Run slim in dry-run or inspection mode first.
Compare generated commands against a checklist before execution.

E_compliance.rationale: Plandex handles model provider API keys and source code, while slim handles certificate private keys, environment variables, and registry credentials. If those data classes are processed under different retention or residency rules, the pair can create a compliance mismatch. No single-agent residency guarantee is documented here, so the risk is inferred and should be treated conservatively.
conditions: IF regulated secrets or private keys are processed by both agents under different retention policies, compliance mismatch exists.
IF EU or other restricted data is routed through external model or registry services, residency obligations may be violated.
mitigations: Classify data before handing it to either agent.
Keep regulated secrets out of external services.
Document retention and deletion rules for both tools.
Use separate environments for regulated and non-regulated workloads.
